## Trusted Advisor

Trusted Advisor checks configurations and recommends improvements across **cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits, and operational excellence**. The old five-category and fixed seven-check descriptions are outdated. Access depends on support-plan entitlement; use the current check reference.

## Trusted Advisor - Support Plans

Basic includes a limited selection of checks. Business Support+, Enterprise Support, and Unified Operations provide broader capabilities; consult the current entitlement documentation.

## AWS Basic Support Plan

Included for all customers. Provides account/billing help, documentation, public service-health information, and community resources. Basic is not a paid technical support plan.

## Current paid support plans

| Plan | Distinguishing capability |
| --- | --- |
| Business Support+ | 24/7 technical support and AWS Support API access |
| Enterprise Support | Designated TAM and response targets for critical production cases |
| Unified Operations | Additional operational engagement, specialist expertise, and critical-workload support |

Compare current severity definitions and response targets on the official plan pages. Targets describe initial response or engagement, not guaranteed incident resolution.

## Legacy support-plan transition

As of this review, Developer Support, the old Business Support, and Enterprise On-Ramp are transition-era plans with a stated end date of **1 January 2027** in the commercial AWS Regions. Existing-customer transition rules differ by plan. AWS documents an exception for AWS GovCloud (US), where these plans remain available. New-account questions should use the current plan lineup rather than the old names.

Current plans are Basic, Business Support+, Enterprise Support, and Unified Operations. Enterprise adds a designated TAM; Unified Operations provides additional operational support. Older Developer, Business, and Enterprise On-Ramp comparisons are historical during the transition to 1 January 2027, with AWS GovCloud (US) exceptions. ## Amazon Sumerian

Historical service: AWS lists Amazon Sumerian as retired, with support ending in March 2023. Its former purpose was building web-based AR/VR and 3D experiences. It is not a current service recommendation.

changes.find: - Applications can communicate with devices even when they aren’t connected
changes.replace: - Device Shadows retain reported/desired state while devices are offline; a disconnected device receives relevant updates after it reconnects, not through a live offline connection.

## Amazon Elastic Transcoder

Historical service: Elastic Transcoder ended support in November 2025. For new file-based media transcoding, evaluate **AWS Elemental MediaConvert**, which converts media into supported delivery formats. Do not select Elastic Transcoder for a new deployment.

changes.find: - Synchronize to Amazon S3 (any storage classes including Glacier), Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx for Windows
changes.replace: - Transfers data to supported S3, EFS, and FSx locations. Archived source objects may need restoration before they can be read; destination storage-class and metadata behavior have service-specific rules.

Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers on 7 November 2025. These capabilities are retained for context; new customers should use the alternatives in AWS's availability guidance.

changes.find: ## AWS Pinpoint

## AWS Pinpoint

End of support is scheduled for **30 October 2026**, after this review date. Plan migration rather than treating its campaign, journey, endpoint, and analytics features as a long-term new-workload choice. The SMS, voice, mobile push, OTP, and number-validation APIs continue under AWS End User Messaging; that is not a blanket replacement for every Pinpoint feature.
